summary: Richard Salomon is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ludo Rocher. He served as a professor at the University of Washington (attested 1998–2017) and held a visiting research post at Soka University in 2007.

Richard Schmidt (1866–1939) was an Indologist who completed his doctorate and habilitation at Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He served as Privatdozent at Halle-Wittenberg (~1898–1906) and became an ordinary professor at Münster in 1910.
Richard Shilleto (1809–1876) was a scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology. He was educated at Repton School, Shrewsbury School (~1823–1828), and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1828–1832).

Richard Sorabji is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Pembroke College (~1953–1957). He taught at Cornell University (~1962–1970), served as professor at King's College London (~1970–2000), and held a post at Gresham College (~2000–2006).

Linguist Richard Sproat earned his degrees at UC San Diego (1977–1981) and MIT (1981–1985). He held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (2003–2009), Oregon Health and Science University (2009–2012), and Google (2012).

Richard Sylvan (1935–1996) was a philosopher who studied at Victoria University of Wellington (~1954–1958) and Princeton University (~1958–1962). He held posts at the University of Sydney (~1963–1965) and as a fellow at Australian National University (1971).

Working in history, archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian, and Buddhist studies, Richard Taupier completed his MS and doctorate at UMass Amherst. He has served as Associate Director of Research Development at UMass Amherst and visiting lecturer at Smith College.

Indologist Richard W. Lariviere studied under Ludo Rocher at the University of Pennsylvania (Ph.D. ~1978). He held posts as professor and dean at UT Austin (~1982–2006), provost at Kansas (2006–2009), and president of Oregon (2009–2011).

Richard Wilhelm (1873–1930) was a sinologist who studied at the University of Tübingen (~1891–1895). He was a visiting professor at Peking University (1923), held the Sinology chair at Goethe University Frankfurt (1924), and founded the university in 1925.

Richard von Garbe (1857–1927) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Rudolf von Roth at Tübingen. He held posts at the University of Königsberg (1878–1894) and succeeded Roth as chairholder at Tübingen (1895–1927).

Richard von Glahn is a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology. He became a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1987) and served as a visiting fellow at the University of Tokyo (1988–1989).
Rigdzin Shikpo (1935–2023) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Chögyam Trungpa and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.

Riika J. Virtanen is a scholar of Tibetology who conducted doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki under Asko Parpola, Klaus Karttunen, and Hannu K. Riikonen, and also studied under Sangye Tandar Naga.
Rikizan Ishikawa (1943–1997) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa University (~1962–1971) and later served there as Professor of Buddhist Studies (~1974–1997).

Ringu Tulku is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at CIHTS, Namgyal Institute, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, trained under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse and the 16th Karmapa, and founded Bodhicharya.
Rinzin Thargyal was a Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Oslo, completing a Magister degree by 1985 under the supervision of Fredrik Barth and Arne Martin Klausen.

Rita Langer is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Hamburg (2004) under Lambert Schmithausen, also studying at SOAS and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies. She held a post at Bristol (2009).

Rita M. Gross (1943–2015) was a scholar of religion and Buddhist studies who completed her doctorate at Chicago (~1975). She taught at UW-Eau Claire (~1979–2015) and was attested as an assistant professor at UW-Madison in 1990.

Rizong Sras Rinpoche (1927–2022) was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar who studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery (1950–1959). He later served as Abbot of Gyume Tantric Monastery (~1979–1984), Drepung Loseling (1984), and Samstanling Monastery.

Rob Linrothe, a Tibetology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar, earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1992). He held posts at the National Palace Museum, Skidmore College (1992–2009), Rubin Museum of Art, and Northwestern University (2010–2022).
